root_cause: Multiple keydown event listeners are attached to the input field each time the suggestion list is regenerated (e.g., after typing additional characters). The previous listeners are not removed, causing multiple handlers to fire on key events. On Enter, a stale listener from the previous list state clicks an outdated item (Blueberry) after the current listener clicks the correct item (Blackberry), and due to event listener ordering the stale listener's click wins, resulting in the wrong value being set.
repair_strategy: Modify the navigation controller to store a reference to the active keydown listener on the config object and remove any existing listener before attaching a new one. Also update the listener cleanup when the list is not found (e.g., on ESC).
expected_accessibility_effect: Ensures that keyboard navigation (arrow keys, Enter) consistently selects the currently highlighted suggestion, preventing stale listeners from overriding the correct selection. This improves reliability for keyboard-only users and screen reader users who rely on aria-activedescendant and aria-selected.
functional_risks: Minimal; only affects the autoComplete's keyboard navigation. Could affect custom navigation functions if they rely on multiple listeners, but the pattern is to have one.
verification_requirements: Run the journey again to confirm that pressing Enter after filtering selects the highlighted suggestion (Blackberry).
Test ESC key closes list and removes listener.
Verify that rapid typing and arrow navigation does not cause duplicate listeners.
